description: Shared model universe for the openswarm vs oh-my-openagent routing benchmark. Every id appears in both pinned trees: OpenCode Go and DeepSeek ids are keys of openswarm policy.json (ocgo.monthly_limits.go or deepseek.tiers) and strings in oh-my-openagent packages/model-core (category fallback chains or supplemental capability entries). Codex slugs are not pinned by openswarm (it classifies live `codex debug models` output); most slugs below are named by model-core; the configured OpenSwarm default gpt-6-luna is also included as an illustrative available model. Descriptions are classified by policy.json tier_keywords.
provider_notes: chatgpt-subscription stands in for the Codex/ChatGPT plan. The openai API provider is not connected: this comparison is one Codex subscription, not a second metered OpenAI key.
opencode-go is the OpenCode Go plan. opencode (Zen), github-copilot, anthropic, google, xai, zai-coding-plan, xiaomi, moonshotai and kimi-for-coding are not connected.
deepseek is the metered DeepSeek API.
openswarm exclude_patterns (minimax, luna, preview, ...) still apply on the openswarm side. OmO does not read that list, so an excluded Go model stays reachable for OmO.

policy.json maps both balanced and deep onto deepseek-v4-pro. The catalogue tier is deep, so a balanced task that lands here counts as over-provisioned. OmO unspecified-low lists providers deepseek and opencode-go on one rung; the first connected provider is deepseek, and a failed rung does not hop to the next provider on that same entry.
